aspects.says: Cloning an ISOMsg gives a separate message, so changing the clone leaves the original as it was.
When the message cannot be handled, the participant puts the ISOException in the Context and returns ABORTED instead of letting it escape.
basis: section:6.3 Integrating Data Element Handling in a jPOS Server

aspects.says: A single data element can be handled on its own as an ISOField carrying its field number and value.
aspects.reason: the page's own words: you usually work through ISOMsg; splitting the value on a pipe is plain Java, not a jPOS idea

aspects.says: A response is built from its request: it keeps the request's data elements, takes the matching response MTI through setResponseMTI, and adds the response code (39) and authorization code (38).
